mainTopic: Whether the משנה or the ברייתא gives רבי יוסי's view on an אנדרוגינוס, and the cases where רב and שמואל rule like רבי יוסי.
overview: The משנה quotes רבי יוסי (with רבי שמעון) saying that an אנדרוגינוס כהן lets his wife eat תרומה, but a ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי alone saying an אנדרוגינוס is a creature of his own kind, never ruled male or female. The first opinion follows the ברייתא, because רבי יוסי left his partner and so must have changed his mind. שמואל keeps the משנה instead. The גמרא explains that although שמואל usually takes lone opinions into account, he does not do so when it would uproot a משנה. Next, the school of רב says the הלכה follows רבי יוסי on אנדרוגינוס and grafting, while שמואל says it follows him on hard labor (קושי) and forfeiture (קידוש). The גמרא explains each case: grafting before שביעית, where רב נחמן adds thirty extra days to every opinion's rooting time; and how long hard labor can last, where רבי יוסי says two weeks. It then begins the קידוש case of a vine spread over a friend's grain, and רבי יוסי's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה gives way to the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion states that our משנה's version of רבי יוסי cannot stand against a ברייתא that says otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not followed when a ברייתא disagrees with it.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא rules that the משנה's report of רבי יוסי's view is set aside in favor of a ברייתא. The next step brings that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has רבי יוסי saying an אנדרוגינוס כהן lets his wife eat תרומה. This opinion says not to rely on that report, because another source records רבי יוסי differently.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not stand (it is not relied upon)
Our משנה
In the face of / against
A teaching of the תנאים that was left out of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Usually a משנה carries more weight than a ברייתא. This opinion is unusual, and the גמרא will soon ask about exactly that.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah does not stand
in the face of the baraita,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's version of רבי יוסי is set aside in favor of the ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a hermaphrodite is a category of his own
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי saying that an אנדרוגינוס is a unique creature, and the חכמים never decided whether he is male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי says an אנדרוגינוס is a creature of his own kind, and the חכמים did not decide whether he is male or female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that the first opinion relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי treats the אנדרוגינוס like a male כהן whose wife eats תרומה. In this ברייתא he says we cannot know which he is. That contradicts the משנה, so one of the two reports must give way.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with both male and female features
A creature in its own category
Decided

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
A hermaphrodite is a creature unto himself,
and the Sages did not determine about him
whether he is male or female.

steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה gives way to a ברייתא here
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי calls the אנדרוגינוס a creature of his own kind

steps.title: Shouldn't the משנה win instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first opinion: why not set aside the ברייתא in favor of the משנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Let the ברייתא give way to the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and asks why the ranking was not reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is normally the stronger source. Preferring a ברייתא over it needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary

phrases.english: On the contrary, the baraita does not stand
in the face of the Mishnah!

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the ברייתא beats the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה normally outranks a ברייתא, so the ranking should be the other way around.

steps.title: רבי יוסי left his partner, so he changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה, רבי יוסי rules together with רבי שמעון. In the ברייתא he stands alone, which shows he took back his earlier view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי יוסי left his partner, learn from this that he changed his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא wins in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון together, while the ברייתא gives only רבי יוסי. That suggests the ברייתא records his later view, after he changed his mind. His later view outweighs the usual rule that a משנה is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: He left him
His partner (here, רבי שמעון)
He went back on his view
Learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: According to this first opinion, the ברייתא shows רבי יוסי's final view: an אנדרוגינוס is a doubtful case of his own kind.

phrases.english: From the fact that Rabbi Yosei left his partner,
phrases.notes: His partner is רבי שמעון, who rules with him in the משנה.

phrases.english: learn from this that he retracted.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Special circumstance overrides the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A משנה should always beat a ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here the ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי retracted, so it wins.

steps.title: שמואל: the ברייתא gives way to the משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל takes the opposite view: the ברייתא is set aside and the משנה stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: the ברייתא does not stand against the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, שמואל, disagrees and keeps the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the normal ranking holds, so the משנה's version of רבי יוסי is followed.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
The baraita does not stand in the face of the Mishnah.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is followed, and the ברייתא is set aside.

steps.title: But שמואל worries about lone opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: שמואל is known to take even a lone opinion into account, so why not here?
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, the משנה should give way to the ברייתא, since we know that שמואל takes a lone opinion into account!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל using his own known approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere שמואל takes even a single dissenting view seriously. The ברייתא here is that kind of lone view, so we would expect him to take it into account.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard about him
He takes into account / is concerned about
A lone (minority) opinion

phrases.english: On the contrary, the Mishnah does not stand
in the face of the baraita,
for we have heard that Shmuel
takes into account an individual opinion!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the ברייתא is set aside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל elsewhere takes lone opinions into account, so he should take this ברייתא into account too.

steps.title: Not when it would uproot the משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל takes a lone opinion into account only when it adds to the משנה, not when it would cancel the משנה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only when the משנה is not uprooted. When the משנה would be uprooted, he does not take it into account.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits שמואל's rule about lone opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lone view can be added as an extra concern alongside the משנה. Here, though, following the ברייתא would overturn the משנה's ruling completely, so שמואל keeps the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only (when)
Is uprooted

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's concern for lone opinions stops where it would overturn a משנה.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, כִּי לָא מִתְעַקְרָא מַתְנִיתִין,
phrases.english: This applies only when the Mishnah is not uprooted,
but when the Mishnah is uprooted,
he does not take it into account.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל always takes lone opinions into account.
steps.terutzMaskana: He does so only when the משנה is not uprooted.

steps.title: Where the הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The school of רב says the הלכה follows רבי יוסי on אנדרוגינוס and grafting. שמואל says it follows him on protracted labor and forfeiture.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב said in רב's name: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי on an אנדרוגינוס and on grafting. שמואל said: on protracted labor and on forfeiture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records two lists of cases where the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's list includes אנדרוגינוס. רש"י explains that this follows רבי יוסי of the משנה, since in all these cases רבי שמעון rules with him. So it argues with the earlier statement in רב's name that the ברייתא wins. שמואל lists other cases instead.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (students) of רב
Grafting
Protracted, difficult labor
Forfeiture (of mixed growth in a vineyard)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי on אנדרוגינוס and הרכבה. שמואל: on קושי and קידוש.

phrases.english: The school of Rav said in the name of Rav:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei
regarding a hermaphrodite and regarding grafting,
and Shmuel said: regarding protracted labor and regarding forfeiture.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב and שמואל each name different areas where the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בי רב in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי on אנדרוגינוס and הרכבה. שמואל: on קושי and קידוש.

steps.title: Explaining the cases of אנדרוגינוס and grafting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first two cases where דבי רב rule like רבי יוסי. אנדרוגינוס was already discussed. הרכבה refers to a משנה about grafting before שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of the אנדרוגינוס is what we already discussed. The case of grafting is from this משנה: One may not plant, bend a vine into the ground, or graft in the year before שביעית if less than thirty days remain before ראש השנה. If he did, he must uproot it. רבי יהודה says: a graft that does not take hold within three days never will. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: two weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two cases that דבי רב mentioned in Step 8. It points back for אנדרוגינוס, and quotes a משנה for grafting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that a plant put in at the end of the sixth year might take root in שביעית. The opinions argue about how long a plant needs to take root: the first view says thirty days, רבי יהודה says three days, and רבי יוסי with רבי שמעון say two weeks. Since the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, two weeks is the measure for rooting.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with both male and female features
Grafting one plant onto another
Bending a vine branch into the ground so it takes root
The end of the sixth year, just before the seventh (שמיטה) year
Takes hold or takes root

phrases.english: The androgynous: that which we said.
Grafting: as we learned in a Mishnah:
One may not plant, and one may not sink a vine branch into the ground,
and one may not graft, on the eve of the Sabbatical Year

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
phrases.english: less than thirty days before Rosh HaShana.
And if he planted, sank, or grafted, he must uproot it.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַרְכָּבָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ קוֹלֶטֶת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים
phrases.english: Any graft that does not take hold within three days
will no longer take hold.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים: שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say: two weeks.
phrases.notes: Here שבתות means weeks, not Shabbos days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the sources for the two cases דבי רב listed in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The grafting case is the משנה in שביעית, where רבי יוסי says a plant takes root within two weeks.

steps.title: Each number is added on top of thirty extra days
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, explains that each opinion's rooting time is added to another thirty days before ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The one who says thirty needs thirty plus thirty. The one who says three needs three plus thirty. The one who says two weeks needs two weeks plus thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains how to read the numbers in the משנה. Each opinion's time for rooting is added to an extra thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last thirty days of the sixth year are already treated like שביעית, so a plant must finish rooting before those thirty days begin. So the first view forbids planting sixty days before ראש השנה, רבי יהודה thirty-three days, and רבי יוסי two weeks plus thirty days. Following רבי יוסי, the deadline is forty-four days before ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
Requires, needs
Thirty plus thirty: time to take root plus the extra thirty days

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה's 'thirty days' as the whole deadline. רב נחמן teaches that every opinion's number sits on top of an additional thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
According to the one who says thirty,
thirty and thirty are required.
phrases.notes: Thirty days for the plant to root, and thirty more because the last thirty days of the sixth year already count like שביעית.

phrases.english: According to the one who says three,
three and thirty are required.
According to the one who says two weeks,
two weeks and thirty are required.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to apply the numbers in the משנה quoted in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each opinion's rooting time is added to thirty extra days before ראש השנה of שביעית.

steps.title: שמואל's cases: first, how long hard labor lasts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to שמואל's cases, קושי and קידוש, and explains קושי from a משנה about how long a woman's hard labor can last.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי in hard labor and in forfeiture. Hard labor is from this משנה: How long can her hard labor last? רבי מאיר says: forty or fifty days. רבי יהודה says: her month is enough. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: hard labor does not last more than two weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to שמואל's half of the ruling and starts explaining his first case, קושי, by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bleeding during hard labor is linked to the birth, so it does not make the woman a זבה. The question is how far back before the birth this applies: forty or fifty days, the month of the birth, or two weeks. שמואל rules like רבי יוסי, so the limit is two weeks; קידוש will be explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: Hard, drawn-out labor before giving birth
Here: produce becoming forbidden (forfeited), not marriage
The period of hard labor
Her month is enough for her

steps.whatToRemember: In both grafting and hard labor, רבי יוסי's number is two weeks. בי רב rule like him on grafting, and שמואל rules like him on hard labor.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: in protracted labor and forfeiture.
phrases.notes: קידוש here means something becoming forbidden, not marriage; the גמרא explains it after this.

phrases.english: Protracted labor: as we learned in a Mishnah:
How long can her protracted labor be?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אוֹ אַרְבָּעִים אוֹ חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: either forty or fifty days.
Rabbi Yehuda says: her month is enough for her.
phrases.notes: He means the month in which she gives birth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
Protracted labor does not last more than two weeks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the explanation of דבי רב's cases and returns to שמואל's cases from Step 8, starting with קושי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of קושי, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: hard labor lasts no more than two weeks.

steps.title: Explaining קידוש: a vine spread over a friend's grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the קידוש case by quoting a משנה. A man spreads his grapevine over his friend's grain. רבי מאיר says this makes the grain forbidden, and the vine owner must pay for the loss. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון then begin to state their opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is קידוש? As we learned in a משנה: If someone spreads his grapevine over his friend's grain, he has made the grain forbidden, and he must pay for the loss. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now explaining קידוש, the second case where שמואל rules like רבי יוסי, by bringing the משנה it comes from. The step ends as רבי יוסי's side is introduced, so it is setting up his opinion, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain growing under a grapevine becomes forbidden as כלאי הכרם. רבי מאיר holds the vine owner caused this, so the grain is forbidden and he must pay his friend. The opening words of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון show they disagree. Their view, which שמואל follows, is given next.

keyTerms.meaning: Making produce forbidden through כלאי הכרם, so nobody may use it
One who spreads something over, like a covering (here, a vine over grain)
Forbidden mixture of grapevines with grain or vegetables
Grain
Responsibility to pay for a loss

steps.confusionAlert: Here קידוש does not mean marriage or making something holy. It means the grain becomes forbidden because it is mixed with a vineyard.

phrases.english: Proscription — as we learned in a mishna:
One who spreads his grapevine
over the grain of his fellow —
he has proscribed it,
phrases.notes: He means the grain is now forbidden as כלאי הכרם, a vine-and-grain mixture.

phrases.english: and he is responsible for it,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining קושי in step 11, the גמרא moves to שמואל's second case, קידוש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: someone who spreads his vine over a friend's grain makes it forbidden and must pay for it. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון disagree (their view follows).
